title: StateMirror: Pre-Execution Detection of Hallucinated Tool Calls in Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.32648v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based coding agents may propose invalid actions that are not applicable in the execution environment, such as accessing non-existent paths or missing packages. We term this mismatch hallucinated tool use. A preliminary study of 4,398 agent trajectories reveals that these hallucinations are pervasive and costly, requiring a median of 3 additional interaction steps and 22.4K tokens to recover. Existing frameworks rely on reactive, post-execution feedback, wasting runtime resources. Nevertheless, since an agent's execution environment is grounded in concrete codebase and harness components, many action prerequisites can be extracted and validated prior to execution. To this end, we introduce StateMirror, a lightweight pre-execution detector. StateMirror intercepts actions at the harness boundary, extracts state predicates via AST and command analysis, and deterministically validates them against the live repositor

translated_title: StateMirror：编码智能体中幻觉工具调用的执行前检测
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的编码智能体可能会提出在执行环境中不适用的无效操作，例如访问不存在的路径或缺失的软件包。我们将这种不匹配称为“幻觉工具使用”（hallucinated tool use）。一项针对4,398条智能体轨迹的初步研究表明，这类幻觉现象普遍存在且代价高昂，恢复它们平均需要3次额外的交互步骤和22.4K个token。现有框架依赖于被动式的执行后反馈机制，浪费了运行时资源。然而，由于智能体的执行环境建立在具体的代码库和工具框架（harness）组件之上，许多操作的前提条件可以在执行之前被提取并加以验证。为此，我们提出了StateMirror，一个轻量级的执行前检测器。StateMirror在工具框架边界拦截操作，通过AST（抽象语法树）和命令分析提取状态谓词，并针对实时代码库对其进行确定性验证。
tldr: 提出StateMirror，一个轻量级执行前检测器，通过在工具框架边界拦截操作、利用AST和命令分析提取状态谓词并对照实时代码库进行确定性验证，从而在执行之前检测出编码智能体的幻觉工具调用，避免了现有执行后反馈机制对运行时资源的浪费。
